# `scope_get_ra_dec`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the mount's current right ascension and declination, falling back to the last synchronised pair when no live position is available.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build: C / MUTATOR established independently, full contract parity unresolved) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x79040 (64-bit guider build); driver GetCoordinates @0xeeb20, GetRaDec @0x698f0; 32-bit handler @0x72b9c |

No parameters are read. With a connected, position-capable mount the handler queries the controller for the coordinates, updates tracking state (so a ScopeTrack event can follow) and reads a third value, appended to the result unless it is the -999 sentinel (local sidereal time, INFERRED). Otherwise it returns the cached pair from the last sync, provided the cached values are not within 0.1 of the -999 sentinel; if there is neither, the request fails with 207. A failed live read increments shared failure counters; after repeated or elapsed failures the guider asks the main imager whether autosave is running and can install a callback that stops capture and marks the mount disconnected, or run the communication-failure handler. This getter therefore has operational recovery paths and is graded as a mutator. Live-versus-cached reliability and the coordinate epoch are unresolved. Mount serial (firmware 9.31, READ): :GR and :GD.

Side effects: Reads the mount controller; updates shared tracking state and failure counters; after repeated failures may trigger capture stop, a mount-disconnected notice or the communication-failure handler.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"scope_get_ra_dec"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 207 | No live coordinates and no valid cached pair (the failure code is unassigned by the handler) | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

The handler has no explicit numeric error branch of its own; driver errors are forwarded. Further branches forward an error code set by the mount driver or a helper; the codes are not exhausted by this table.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":71,"method":"scope_get_ra_dec"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_get_ra_dec","result":[5.5,20.25,7.125],"code":0,"id":71}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_get_ra_dec","error":"fail to operate","code":207,"id":72}
```
